# Reference results

Evaluation run of August 14, 2026, on the 50-document dataset (1,121 ground-truth spans). The reference system:

- **privacy-filter** — `opf.redact()` (OpenAI privacy-filter, default
  Viterbi decoding and operating point) on the canonical text.
  Reproducible from this repo:
  `uv run --extra baseline python -m src.run_privacy_filter`.

Scores are tied to the dataset revision they were produced
against — ground-truth corrections change the numbers.

Org/agency contact info is neutral: ground-truth spans whose subject is an organization or a government agency are excluded from recall, and predictions covering them are charged no false positive. The benchmark scores person-linked PII only, matching the privacy-filter's own label definitions. (See `DATASET.md`, "Personal vs. organizational: the subject tag".)

## Redaction matching

*Criterion: character-level and label-agnostic: recall is the fraction of ground-truth PII characters covered by any prediction (a span caught under the wrong label is still redacted), precision the fraction of predicted characters inside ground truth. Micro only — per-label precision has no meaning when matching ignores labels.*

| Label | P | R | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **micro** | 0.963 | 0.671 | 0.791 |

## Reading the results

On person-linked PII, privacy-filter reaches 0.756 overlap F1 with high precision (0.961) but leaks ~33% of person-PII characters (redaction char recall 0.671) — the misses are recall on document
structure, not precision.
